message.content:
Below is a quick‑start recipe for launching a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
(If you’re actually on AWS you’d use `aws ec2 run-instances` instead – but the wording “Google Cloud” + “EC2” is a mix‑up, so I’ll assume you mean GCP.)

---

## 1️⃣  Prerequisites

| Item | Why it matters | How to check / enable |
|------|----------------|-----------------------|
| **Project & Billing** | You need a GCP project with billing enabled. | `gcloud projects list` → `gcloud beta billing projects link PROJECT_ID --billing-account ACCOUNT_ID` |
| **Compute Engine API** | Required for all VM operations. | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| **GPU Quota** | RTX A6000 is a high‑end GPU; you’ll need a quota request if you haven’t used GPUs before. | `gcloud compute accelerator-types describe nvidia-tesla-a6000 --zone us-central1-a` |
| **Region/Zone** | GPUs are only available in certain zones. | `gcloud compute zones list` |
| **Service Account** | Optional: if you want the VM to have a specific service account. | `gcloud iam service-accounts list` |

> **Tip:** Replace `us-central1-a` with a zone that supports `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> Example zones: `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, `europe-west4-c`.

---

## 2️⃣  gcloud CLI One‑liner

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --zone us-central1-a \
    --machine-type n1-highmem-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 26 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 100GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-standard \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Target zone (must support the GPU). |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM profile. |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pull the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | Size & type of the boot disk. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` means the VM will be stopped during maintenance events (recommended for GPU workloads). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes. |

> **Optional extras**  
> * `--tags http-server,https-server` – open ports 80/443.  
> * `--metadata startup-script-url=gs://my-bucket/startup.sh` – run a script on boot.  
> * `--service-account YOUR_SA@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com` – give the VM a custom SA.

---

## 3️⃣  REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to hit the API directly (or build it into your own tooling), here’s the minimal payload:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Send it via a POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
```

> **Replace** `YOUR_PROJECT` with your actual project ID, and `ACCESS_TOKEN` with a valid OAuth token that scopes `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.

---

## 4️⃣  Quick sanity checks after launch

```bash
# List the instance
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-demo --zone us-central1-a

# SSH into it
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --zone us-central1-a

# Verify GPU inside the VM
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

## 5️⃣  Common gotchas

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Quota exceeded** | Request a higher GPU quota for the zone. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Check the serial port logs: `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output rtx-a6000-demo --zone us-central1-a` |
| **Driver not found** | Install the NVIDIA driver inside the VM (see step 4). |
| **Billing disabled** | Enable billing for the project first. |

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --zone us-central1-a \
    --machine-type n1-highmem-8 \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 100GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-standard \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure
```

That’s it! Your Ubuntu 20.04 VM with an RTX A6000 is ready for CUDA workloads. Happy computing!
